patch.value: GH-1660: no supported way points opted-in test telemetry at a local collector, and the project telemetry.endpoint that pm init writes is ignored

GitHub issue #1660 (reported 2026-11-04 against 2026.11.4). docs/CONFIGURATION.md 'Test environments' says PM_TELEMETRY_SOURCE_CONTEXT or PM_TELEMETRY_SEND_TEST_EVENTS=1 permits intentional test delivery and tells authors to point such tests at a local collector, but nothing supported does that. No environment variable overrides the event endpoint (SENTRY_DSN redirects Sentry and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_* redirects spans; PM_TELEMETRY_INGEST_KEY is auth only). pm config project/global set telemetry.endpoint refuses with invalid_argument_value. pm init writes a full telemetry block, including the production endpoint, into the project settings.json, yet editing that value has no effect: pm ops telemetry status still reports the production endpoint, because the effective telemetry settings are read from the global profile only (src/core/store/settings.ts resolves endpoint from the global settings). Only hand-editing the global profile changes status.endpoint. Impact: an extension test that followed the documented opt-in delivered its expected refusals to production Sentry (PM-CLI-3R..3X, environment=test), which blocked the 2026.11.4 auto-release Sentry gate; the release-gate side is owned by pm-usn5k2 and the extension side by unbraind/pm-vcs#176. Duplicate check: searched telemetry endpoint/override/local collector/project settings across all statuses; the closed telemetry env-var and pipeline items document the opt-out surface but no endpoint override.

A documented environment override (for example PM_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT) points event delivery at another collector, validated like the settings endpoint and reported in pm ops telemetry status env_overrides; The project-level telemetry block is either honored for the endpoint or no longer written by pm init, and a spec shows status.endpoint matches what actually receives events; docs/CONFIGURATION.md Test environments names the supported override next to SENTRY_DSN and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*
A test that opts into telemetry delivery can point it at a local collector through one documented, supported setting, and pm ops telemetry status reports the endpoint that receives events
No env override exists, config set refuses telemetry.endpoint, and the project telemetry.endpoint written by pm init is silently ignored, so opted-in test events reach production

value.text: Code evidence, verified on feat/sdk-caller-contract (2026.11.4 source). The description's pointer is imprecise: src/core/store/settings.ts buildTelemetrySettings only normalizes whichever file it is given. The global-only behaviour comes from src/core/telemetry/runtime.ts. Every delivery site calls readSettings(globalPmRoot), including ensureInstallationId, which returns the endpoint the queue flush uses. No site reads the project settings, so the project telemetry block that pm init writes is never consulted for the endpoint. Fix direction: one env override that resolves at that seam and is reported in env_overrides, and pm init stops writing the inert project block or documents it as ignored.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Design constraints found while scoping (source of 2026.11.4). (1) Endpoint consumers: src/core/telemetry/runtime.ts ensureInstallationId (feeds every queue flush and the detached flush worker), src/sdk/telemetry.ts buildTelemetryStatusSummary (status.endpoint), and two health probes in src/sdk/governance/health.ts. An override must resolve through one helper used by all of them, or status will disagree with delivery. (2) Queued events (QueuedTelemetryEvent) do not record an endpoint, and the queue is per global profile. Suppose a test sets an override and shares the real global profile, and delivery to the local collector fails. Its events stay queued, and the next ordinary run flushes them to production. The override must either stamp the endpoint on each queued entry and flush per entry, or the docs must require a disposable PM_GLOBAL_PATH beside it. Pending OTel spans already carry a per-span endpoint. (3) An invalid override must fail closed, disabling delivery and reporting it in env_overrides, never fall back to the configured endpoint. A fallback reproduces exactly the incident: the author believes delivery is local while it reaches production. (4) The project telemetry block must not be honored. A cloned repository would otherwise redirect a user's telemetry to an endpoint the repository chose. So the second acceptance criterion resolves as 'no longer written by pm init'. serializeSettings writes the full PmSettings, including telemetry, for every root, so the omission belongs in serialization for project roots, with init fixtures updated.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Consent defect reproduced on the 2026.11.4 build, which has the same root cause as the endpoint report. The setup wizard asks 'Enable telemetry for this project? [Y/n]' and writes the answer only into the project .agents/pm/settings.json (sdk/init.ts createNewInitSettings sets settings.telemetry.enabled and first_run_prompt_completed, then calls writeSettings(params.pmRoot, ...)). The telemetry runtime reads consent only from the global profile, so the answer has no effect. Reproduction in a disposable HOME and PM_GLOBAL_PATH: drive the wizard through a pseudo-terminal, accept the prefix and preset defaults, and answer n. The project file then holds telemetry.enabled=false, while pm ops telemetry status reports enabled=true and configured_enabled=true. Running pm list and pm ops telemetry flush afterwards delivered the queued events: the disposable profile's runtime/telemetry/state.json recorded last_successful_flush_at with queue_entries=0 against the production endpoint. A user who declines telemetry in the wizard therefore keeps sending it. This relates to the closed revocation work in pm-yjq2x0, which made a global revocation authoritative but never connected the wizard's answer to the global profile. Fix direction: the wizard writes its consent to the global profile, or asks nothing, and the project telemetry block is no longer written.

message: Fourth surface: the documented opt-out command is inert inside a project.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Fourth surface, the most severe. docs/CONFIGURATION.md tells users to opt out persistently with 'pm config set telemetry-tracking off'. The scope-less shorthand resolves to project scope (src/cli/register-setup.ts resolveConfigPositionals: resolvedScope 'project'). Run inside a project on the 2026.11.4 build, it returns scope=project, policy=disabled, changed=true and writes the project file, while pm ops telemetry status keeps configured_enabled=true. The documented opt-out therefore does not opt out for anyone who runs it inside a tracker, which is the normal place to run pm. Fix: the scope-less shorthand for telemetry-tracking resolves to the global profile, and an explicit project scope refuses with the global command as remedy.

patch.value: Wizard decline: global consent disabled. pm config set telemetry-tracking off: scope global, configured_enabled false. Events under PM_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT reached a local listener, and an invalid value disabled delivery. All of this was checked end to end on the built CLI in a disposable profile, and the specs fail without each fix.
A user's telemetry choice, made through the wizard, the documented opt-out or config, takes effect for the CLI install, and opted-in tests deliver only to the collector PM_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT names

Every project-level telemetry surface was inert, because the runtime reads consent and endpoint only from the global profile. The init wizard now persists its answer with persistGlobalTelemetryConsent and asks only while no consent is recorded and no environment opt-out applies, so it never overrides an earlier choice. writeSettings gains omitSections, which never removes a section the stored file already has. defaultConfigScope routes a scope-less telemetry-tracking call, from the CLI shorthand or MCP, to the global profile. Project-scope get and set refuse with invalid_argument_value (reason telemetry_consent_is_global), and project list and export omit the key, so ConfigResult.values is Partial. Health reads the global profile. PM_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT accepts only absolute http(s) URLs, and any other value disables delivery. Override events and delivery state use files keyed by the override (telemetryRuntimeFileName). Each flush resolves the override once, for both file and target. Span state and alias usage stay in the shared state file, and idle override files are pruned after a day. Diagnostics redact endpoint credentials. An independent review agent ran five rounds to zero findings, including two P1 routing defects that round 1 found in an earlier per-entry-stamp design.

Fixed: telemetry consent and the event endpoint live only in the global profile. The init wizard records its answer there and writes no project telemetry block. The scope-less telemetry-tracking shorthand and MCP target the global profile, and project scope refuses. PM_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT points opted-in tests at a local collector through an isolated queue.

value.text: PR 1661 review follow-up (CodeRabbit, 4 findings in this item's scope) fixed on the same branch. (1) The init wizard re-checks consent after its prompt. If another process recorded a choice while the prompt was open, that choice stands and init warns telemetry_consent_kept:recorded_while_prompting. The write reconciles against that re-read under the settings lock, and an unreadable global profile is never asked about, matching the runtime first-use prompt. (2) The init result, its concise summary and its display line report the global profile's telemetry block, the one the runtime reads, instead of the project default enabled=true. (3) pm health --check-telemetry sends URL credentials of the endpoint (PM_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT or configured) as a Basic authorization header, because fetch refuses a URL with userinfo while event delivery through http.request accepts one. (4) A malformed shared state.json now raises telemetry_state_invalid_json even when an endpoint override reads its own state file. Specs: init-command (3 new cases), health-command (2 new cases), all passing. The remaining missing-file race, where a write from a read that found no settings.json replaces a file created meanwhile, is reproduced and filed as pm-nroemi.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: PR 1661, independent review agent round on the CodeRabbit fixes (8 findings, all addressed on the branch). (1) P2: the init result had started to carry the whole global telemetry block, so pm init --json and --verbose printed the global endpoint with any URL credentials and the installation id. The result now takes only enabled, first_run_prompt_completed and capture_level from the global profile, and a spec asserts that neither secret appears. (2) The consent re-check is now atomic. WriteSettingsOptions gains skipIfStored, a compare-and-set consulted under the settings lock with the stored document. The wizard write skips when a choice is already stored, which also covers a profile created by another process after the re-read, and warns telemetry_consent_kept:recorded_while_prompting. A profile that became unreadable during the prompt is left alone, with the warning telemetry_consent_not_recorded:global_settings_unreadable. When init targets the global profile itself, the create write still records the answer, and that missing-file case stays with pm-nroemi. (3) The health probe decodes userinfo with a fallback for malformed escapes, always strips it from the probe URL, and redacts the probe URL and any URL credentials from transport error messages. redactTelemetryEndpoint now also strips credentials, query and fragment from text that is not a valid URL, through the new shared stripUrlCredentials. The SDK surface acknowledges the WriteSettingsOptions signature change.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: PR 1661, third review round (CodeRabbit, 4 findings in this item's scope), fixed. flushQueue now records a PM_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT override redacted in its state file, without credentials, query or fragment, through recordedStateEndpoint; delivery still posts to the real endpoint, and the configured-endpoint state is unchanged. A spec flushes a credentialed, tokenised override and checks the state file. docs/CONFIGURATION.md now states that pm telemetry clear revokes consent and deletes every telemetry queue and state file of the profile, and that an empty PM_TELEMETRY_ENDPOINT uses the configured endpoint while any other non-URL value disables delivery. docs/SDK.md adds migration guidance for the two acknowledged breaking SDK entries: WriteSettingsOptions gains optional omitSections and skipIfStored, and ConfigResult.values is Partial because project scope omits telemetry_tracking. The pm-nroemi description now limits its snapshot claim to successful reads of a valid settings.json. Verification: quality:static passes, and focused v8 coverage is 100 percent for runtime.ts (572/572 branches) and policy.ts.
